title: Plan your big day, make a space.
format_note: A customer, Beverly, talks to camera about her Muse wedding-planning space; a 28 s phone screen recording sits mid-film, with an interview frame and a store end card.
one_thing: A real person shows one personal dashboard built in Muse, so the viewer sees that a space is something they could make for their own life.

transcript.voice_style: Warm, unscripted-sounding first person; short sentences with 'Here's…' pointers; a smile in the delivery at t=14 and t=54 (f0007, f0029).
transcript.script_shape: Intro (who, what), problem as a spoken list, 'I asked Muse', three 'Here's…' demo pointers, a change-by-prompt claim, sidebar habit, emotional payoff, invitation line.

structure.frame0: f0001.jpg: white studio ground, soft-fur mascot at left (about 60% of frame height), 'FEATURED SPACE / Wedding Planner / Built by Beverly with her Muse' at right. A poster with the subject in it.
structure.first_3s: Native strip window-01 shows the mascot gone at 0.125 s, walking in from the left by 0.2 s and settling by 0.7 s; the 'Mus' wordmark writes on near t=2 (f0002.jpg). Title text never moves.

beats.what: Mascot title card: 'Wedding Planner, built by Beverly with her Muse'; wordmark writes on and mascot waves by 4.4 s (strips/window-05).
Beverly on camera in four shots (cuts 4.96, 6.96, 9.97, 11.97): 'I'd like to show you a space I created in Muse.'
Five cuts in 4.2 s while she lists 'RSVPs, vendors, invoices, emails, it's all everywhere.' The problem is spoken, not shown.
Hard cut to a phone on a blue gradient: 'Beverly & Forrest', '319 days to go', four stat tiles; she asked Muse for a dashboard.
Tap on RSVP; the view lands with 24 / 43 / 27 / 3 tiles and a guest list with status chips (f0014, f0015).
Tap on Vendors; budget page, $24,200 total cost, $17,825 still owed, line items (f0016, f0017).
Tap on Recent email; email summaries with 'Needs reply' chips, '4 threads are waiting on a reply' (f0018-f0020).
Dashboard scrolls back to the top while she says changes are made by telling Muse; no prompt interface appears.
Menu button tap; drawer slides in with the wedding tab highlighted, then closes back to the dashboard (strips/window-36).
Back to Beverly in six shots with a cut every 1.1-3 s: 'takes the stress out of something that should honestly be really fun.'
Black end card: app icon, 'Muse', Google Play and App Store badges, Meta logo fading up (f0029, f0030).

hero_moment.what: The cut to the phone: dashboard with the magenta '319 days to go' tile, phone about 650 px tall in a 720 px frame (f0011.jpg).

ending.cta_text: Muse; Get it on Google Play; Download on the App Store
ending.what: Centred app icon and wordmark on black above two store badges; Meta logo dim at 56 s, full at 58 s. The spoken invitation ends before the card.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Fast cuts in the interview halves (median shot 1.88 s) around one 28.32 s uninterrupted phone shot (46.7% of runtime). One burst of 5 cuts at 15.1-19.31 s, centred at 28% of runtime, lines up with the spoken list.

look.accent_use: Magenta only on the ampersand in 'Beverly & Forrest', the '319' and the active filter; the Muse blue appears only on logos. The interface alternates pink and mint chips.
look.type: Title card: neutral humanist sans, dark slate headline over a grey subline, small blue all-caps eyebrow. Phone UI: Roboto-like sans, bold names and numbers, grey secondary text.

good.observation: Frame 0 is a poster: mascot, eyebrow, title and credit are all on screen at t=0 and the mascot moves within 0.2 s.
Every tap draws a ripple on the control, the camera pushes in about 1.27x, and the new page lands within a second, so the viewer follows cause and effect.
The UI changes on the narrated phrase: 'Here's the RSVP list' at 24 s has the RSVP tap, 'what we owe each vendor' at 30 s has the Vendors tap, 'emails' at 34 s has the email tap.
The 5-cut burst falls on the spoken list 'RSVPs, vendors, invoices, emails', so the editing pace echoes the clutter being described.
Accent restraint inside the UI: one magenta ampersand and one large '319' make the hero card read in a glance at phone width.
Interview set alternates a wide and a close framing of the same take, so cuts feel natural without b-roll.
The end card is clean: icon, wordmark, two badges, 4.5 s hold, with the Meta logo fading up last.

weak.observation: The claim 'I just tell Muse and it makes the change' has no picture; the screen shows a dashboard scrolling back to the top and a menu, not a prompt being typed.
The problem is only spoken over an interview; nothing on screen shows scattered RSVPs, invoices or emails.
Body text in the phone is about 11-14 px on a 720 px frame, and the phone is 24.7% of frame width, leaving two gradient flanks each about 37% wide empty for 28 s.
A 28.32 s single shot (46.7% of runtime) shows only pushes and scrolls; the voice carries the variety.
The drawer header reads 'Meep' and the active tab label is cut to 'Wedding September 2…', which muddles the brand name.

rule_candidates.rule: For a person-led film, put the person on camera within 5 s, after a 5 s poster card whose subject is already in frame at t=0.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001 poster, first interview cut at 4.96 s

rule_candidates.rule: Cut the problem list at the pace of the spoken words: one cut per list item, 5 cuts in about 4 s, even when the problem has no visual.
An interview-led film may use hard cuts for every shot seam if each cut lands on a phrase boundary; it need not hold to a third hard cuts.
rule_candidates.evidence: all 15 shot seams are hard cuts; cuts on onset 0.333 vs chance 0.193

rule_candidates.rule: Mark each demo tap with a ripple about 100 px wide on a 720 px frame and push the camera in about 1.27x until the new page has landed.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0013, f0016, f0017: phone width 316 px to 402 px

rule_candidates.rule: Start each demo tap on the phrase that names it; the UI follows the voice within 1 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: tap at 24 s on 'Here's the RSVP list', 30 s on vendors, 34 s on emails

rule_candidates.rule: A device mockup at 90% of frame height satisfies the hero size, but its side margins (about 37% of width each) fail the quarter-empty limit unless something fills them.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0011.jpg: phone 316 px wide in 1280 px

rule_candidates.rule: A voice-led film can sit at -16.3 LUFS integrated with true peak -2 dBTP and a short-term peak of -13.8; only the true-peak limit then constrains the mix.
If the voice claims a capability, the picture must show it; a claim with only an idle dashboard on screen leaves the must-carry fact unshown.
rule_candidates.evidence: 'tell Muse and it makes the change' at 38-42 s versus f0021
